root_cause.text: The nested_mmus array reallocation in kvm_vcpu_init_nested() was performed under only kvm->arch.config_lock, but the array is walked under kvm->mmu_lock, allowing a concurrent MMU notifier to access freed memory.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states that the array is walked under kvm->mmu_lock (e.g., from kvm_unmap_gfn_range()), yet the reallocation and freeing only held kvm->arch.config_lock, causing a use-after-free race. The patch fixes this by performing the swap under kvm->mmu_lock and allocating/freeing outside.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix potential race condition and avoid unnecessary reallocation by conditionally resizing the nested MMU array under lock
intent_record.what: Replaced unconditional kvrealloc with conditional kvcalloc when num_mmus exceeds current size, added write_lock on kvm->mmu_lock during memcpy and pointer update, and moved pointer adjustment into the locked section with explicit swap and free.
intent_record.how: The reallocation now only occurs if the required number of MMUs is larger than the current size, avoiding unnecessary memory operations. The copy and back-pointer updates are performed under kvm->mmu_lock to prevent races with concurrent accesses. The old array is freed after swapping, and the loop to initialize new MMUs remains unchanged.

grouping_result.intent: Fix potential race condition and avoid unnecessary reallocation by conditionally resizing the nested MMU array under lock

relevance_review.reason: The group directly addresses the root cause by fixing the locking during nested_mmus array reallocation to prevent a race condition with the MMU notifier.

candidates.rationale: This line initiates the reallocation of the nested_mmus array under only config_lock, without holding mmu_lock, allowing a concurrent MMU notifier to access freed memory if the memory is freed during reallocation.
This swap updates the nested_mmus pointer to the newly allocated memory, while another thread may still be walking the old pointer under mmu_lock, leading to use-after-free.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement initiates the reallocation of the nested_mmus array under only config_lock, without holding mmu_lock. A concurrent MMU notifier that walks the array under mmu_lock can access freed memory if the array is reallocated and the old memory freed.
This swap updates the nested_mmus pointer to the newly allocated memory while another thread may still be walking the old pointer under mmu_lock, leading to a use-after-free condition.
